Invitational|2012]]) }} '''Lamar Alexander Lee Patterson''' (born August 12, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. ==College career== Patterson, a 6'5" [[swingman]] from [[Lancaster, Pennsylvania]], starred at [[J. P. McCaskey High School]], then [[Saint Benedict's Preparatory School]] in [[Newark, New Jersey]]. He chose to play college basketball for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt Panthers]]. During his freshman year, he suffered an ankle injury in a game against [[2009–10 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]] in November 2009 and missed the majority of the season, gaining a [[medical redshirt]].{{cite web | last = Jones| first = Gordie| title = McCaskey product Lamar Patterson redshirting at Pitt | work = [[Lancaster Online]] | date = March 11, 2010 | url = http://lancasteronline.com/sports/mccaskey-product-lamar-patterson-redshirting-at-pitt/article_b67eae62-2baa-5d0b-85e0-fc68e60a39c9.html | access-date = April 13, 2014}} Patterson returned to the court for the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11 season]] and became a key rotation player for the Panthers. As a redshirt sophomore in [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]], Patterson became a starter and raised his scoring average from 2.6 [[points per game]] to 9.6. He finished the season on a high note, as he led the team to the [[2012 College Basketball Invitational]] title. Patterson averaged 13.3 points, 6 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 4.5 [[assists per game]] for the tournament and was named [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]].{{cite web | last = Fittipaldo| first = Ray| title = Pitt's season ends on high note with CBI win | work = [[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] | date = March 31, 2012 | url = https://www.post-gazette.com/home/2012/03/31/Pitt-s-season-ends-on-high-note-with-CBI-win/stories/201203310122 | access-date = April 13, 2014}} As a junior, Patterson helped lead the Panthers back to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. Once there, however, Pitt lost to eventual Final Four participant [[2012–13 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]]. Patterson returned for his senior season as the Panthers moved to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. Patterson enjoyed a breakout season as he was one of the top players in the league, raising his scoring average to 17.1 from 10.0 as a junior.{{cite web| last = DeCourcy| first = Mike| title = Pitt's Lamar Patterson: Focus on performance, not Wooden snub| work = [[Sporting News]]| date = January 26, 2014| url = http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2014-01-26/pitts-lamar-patterson-focus-on-performance-not-wooden-snub| access-date = April 13, 2014| archive-date = April 14, 2014| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140414060249/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2014-01-26/pitts-lamar-patterson-focus-on-performance-not-wooden-snub| url-status = dead}} At the close of the season, Patterson was named second team All-ACC by both the league's coaches and media.{{cite web | last = Zeise| first = Paul| title = Pitt standout Lamar Patterson named second-team All-ACC | work = [[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] | date = March 10, 2014| url = https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2014/03/10/Patterson-named-second-team-All-ACC/stories/201403100196 | access-date = April 13, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Tofas (2014–2015)=== On June 26, 2014, Patterson was selected with the 48th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He was later traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on draft night.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-trade-get-lamar-patterson|title=Hawks Trade To Get Lamar Patterson|date=June 26, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2014}}{{cite web|first=Russell|last=Steinberg|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5848272/lamar-patterson-milwaukee-bucks-nba-draft-results-2014|title=2014 NBA Draft Results: Atlanta Hawks acquire 48th pick Lamar Patterson|date=June 26, 2014|work=SBNation.com|access-date=June 26, 2014}} In July 2014, he joined the Hawks for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].{{cite [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]] (TBL).{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/130255/tofas-bursa-lands-rookie-lamar-patterson.html|title=Tofas Bursa lands On July 31, 2019, Patterson re-signed with the Brisbane Bullets for the [[2019–20 NBL season]].{{cite web|url=http://nbl.com.au/news/article/lamar-patterson-back-with-bullets|title=Lamar Patterson Back with Bullets|work=NBL.com.au|date=July 31, 2019|access-date=July 31, 2019}} He was named to the All-NBL First Team.{{cite news |last1=Gilhooly |first1=Daniel |title=NBL award winners announced |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/28714451/nbl-award-winners-announced |access-date=February 21, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=February 16, 2020}} ===Piratas de Quebradillas (2020)=== On February 16, 2020, Patterson signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/piratas-de-quebradillas-sign-lamar-patterson/|title=Piratas de Quebradillas sign Lamar Patterson|work=sportando.basketball|date=February 17, 2020|access-date=March 27, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} The season was suspended in March due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Puerto Rico|COVID-19 pandemic]]; Patterson re-joined Quebradillas in October 2020 ahead of the season relaunch in November.{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lamar-patterson-re-signs-with-los-piratas-de-quebradillas/|title=Lamar Patterson re-signs with Los Piratas de Quebradillas|work=sportando.basketball|date=October 14, 2020|access-date=October 15, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} He helped Quebradillas reach the BSN Finals, where they lost to [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]].{{cite web|url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/658983/Bayamon-top-Quebradillas-to-claim-BSN-title|title=Bayamon top Quebradillas to claim BSN title|work=latinbasket.com|date=December 18, 2020|access-date=January 5, 2021}} ===New Zealand Breakers (2020–2021)=== On August 4, 2020, Patterson signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] for the [[2020–21 NBL season]], returning to the Australian NBL for a third season.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-sign-lamar-patterson|title=Breakers Sign Lamar Patterson|work=NBL.com.au|date=August 4, 2020|access-date=August 4, 2020}} He struggled early for the Breakers and appeared out of prime playing condition.
